tool_input.task_name: find exact Suzuki coupling records and empirical conditions

key_findings.finding: The standardized reaction is a Suzuki–Miyaura cross-coupling: 3-acetylphenylboronic acid (CC(=O)c1cccc(B(O)O)c1) couples with iodophenol (OC1=CC=C(I)C=C1), replacing the aryl C–I and aryl C–B bonds with a biaryl C–C bond; the phenolic OH and acetyl group remain intact. The standardized product is acetylphenyl–hydroxybiphenyl (CC(=O)c1cccc(-c2ccc(O)cc2)c1).

The reaction database did not return an exact iodophenol match, but returned seven close records using the same acetylphenylboronic acid. These consistently support Pd-catalyzed Suzuki coupling with aryl halides; the closest records use Pd(II) plus fluoride and acetate/base additives, often with a bulky phosphine ligand. Representative sets include Pd(OAc)2 or Pd(II), potassium fluoride, potassium acetate, and a bulky phosphine in THF; and Pd/phosphine with sodium carbonate in ethanol/glyme.

source_tools.relevance: Seven core-reactant Suzuki analog records and listed components
Repeated database search confirming the same analog condition families

key_findings.finding: A practical evidence-grounded condition starting point is a Pd/phosphine Suzuki system with aqueous/inorganic base or acetate/fluoride activation: Pd(OAc)2 or a preformed Pd–phosphine complex (approximately 1–5 mol%), bulky phosphine ligand if Pd(OAc)2 is used, K2CO3/Na2CO3 or KOAc plus KF, and a mixed polar solvent such as THF/water, ethanol/glyme, or related ether/alcohol media. The database extracts supplied no reliable exact temperature, time, or yield for the queried iodophenol substrate, so those parameters should be treated as unverified rather than reported as empirical facts.
